verdict.position: Recommended starting design, not adopted and not closed. Establish: two authored sources in the repository (backlog rows for why, plan directories for what and how), add-only record files beside each plan bound to a digest of the plan's declared files, and one generated committed board of durable facts. Maintain: every change to a source lands with its record, and the board is regenerated in the landing commit on the target; a check in CI fails only the affected plan. Keep healthy: a timer-run, non-LLM sweep reads the board plus run facts kept through fgOS doors and records exceptions. Build it first as tools/plan-supervisor (promoted, with its private parser, TTL lock, home-directory state and claim queue replaced by fgOS doors), measure it on real plans, then plan the move into fgOS.
verdict.confidence: medium on the layering (repository owns portfolio truth, engine owns execution, fgOS doors own run state), which now rests on two owner records and on source read by several seats. Low to medium on the record shapes (D3, D5, D11): they are this seat's answer to the red-team findings; the previous revision of them was examined once and three closures did not hold (RT-4.1, RT-4.2), and the corrections in this revision have been examined by no seat. Low on the continuation rule (D12): it rests on door text that was read and not exercised. The tool-first placement is what makes that acceptable: the shapes are measured before they become fgOS contracts.

design.rule: Two authored sources in the repository; every other portfolio file is a record or generated.
design.detail: Backlog row = intent, authored by the boss. Plan directory = decisions and delivery shape, authored by the shaper then the planner. The canonical link is plan to outcome (`covers` in plan.md frontmatter); the backlog-side view is derived. Ownership is stated per file kind in D8, not as 'one writer each' (that phrase in the first packet contradicted its own role table; red-team RT-3.5).

design.rule: The execution envelope is authored inside plan.md frontmatter.
design.detail: `inputs` (the plan's own files, an explicit list with no patterns; nothing under the plan's `records/` folder and not the board file, both reserved: publishing refuses such an entry, and the digest step skips those paths even if one is listed), `writes` or an explicit read-only marker, `blockedBy`, `covers`, `target`. plan.md is always in the digested subject, so changing any envelope field changes the digest. All reads go through src/util/yaml.mjs readFrontmatter. Day-one reading, made explicit: a plan with no `published` record is `draft` whatever its frontmatter holds, including the 7 plans with no frontmatter at all; required-field checks apply when publishing and to plans that already have a `published` record, where a failure prints `invalid`. readFrontmatter itself returns an empty meta for a missing block (yaml.mjs:91), so the refusal is the tool's check, not the reader's.
design.changed: day-one precedence stated (RT-3.5); records folder and board reserved out of the subject (reviewer/1 finding 1)

design.rule: Records are add-only files named by kind and subject digest, not lines in one shared log.
design.detail: plans/<dir>/records/<kind>-<digest>.json, kinds: published, validated, returned, withdrawn, delivered. A record is never edited or deleted; a new plan revision has a new digest and so new file names. Because a record sits beside the plan, the `records/` folder is never part of the digested subject (D2); otherwise adding a record would change the digest it is named by. A `withdrawn-<digest>` record is final for that digest: it cancels `published`, `validated` and `delivered` at the same digest for every reading in D5 and D6, and the plan comes back only by a revision, which has a new digest. Two worktrees adding records never touch the same file, which removes the concurrent-append question of a shared JSONL (RT-3.5). The digest is taken over the committed bytes of `inputs` at a named commit; publishing refuses a dirty, empty, absolute or symlinked subject, because digestSubject({files}) reads working-tree bytes and accepts all four (ref-digests.mjs:90-96). No `published` record means draft, so the existing plans need no rewrite and no status mapping.
design.changed: per-digest files replace publication.jsonl; digest over committed bytes; records folder outside the subject (reviewer/1 finding 1); what a withdrawn record cancels is stated (RT-4.1)

design.rule: `ready` means published and validated at the same digest, and the validation happens before pickup through an existing door.
design.detail: The first packet narrowed `ready` to 'structurally sound' and accepted wasted launches; the red team is right that this keeps the long lifecycle the owner asked to cut (RT-3.4, RT-3.7). Revised: the validation is a read-only unit through `fgos run` (no --writes, no worktree, no implementation case), pattern solo first as the owner set, a reviewed pattern later. The unit has no write scope and writes only its own report. The validation tick, the non-LLM tool process that called `fgos run` and waited for it to return, reads the settled result and adds the record: `validated-<digest>` holding the unit run id, the base commit and the verdict, or `returned-<digest>` with the report reference when the validation failed. The previous revision said in D4 that the unit writes the record and in D8 that the tick does; the tick is the one writer (RT-4.2). This is an agent claim checked by the tool, weaker than a Workflow receipt (case-projection.mjs isValidReceipt), and the engine still runs judge and validate inside the implementation case (propose.mjs:212-223; inheritFrom refuses another guide or base, case-inherit.mjs:85-88). So the cost today is double validation, measured in P3; removing it is an engine change and stays open.
design.changed: one writer for the validation record: the tick, not the unit (RT-4.2)

design.rule: Delivery is a record written in the landing commit by the landing step, and the dependency test is against the plan's current digest.
design.detail: `delivered-<digest>` = {digest built, case id, evaluator from RECEIPT_EVALUATORS, milestone, passed: true, target}. It is written by the landing step in the commit that lands the change on the target (merge or squash commit), never by a worker and never in a later commit: the runner commits only a unit's declared writes (assignment.mjs, write-scope text near 792-801), so a worker cannot land it, and a later hand commit would survive a revert (RT-3.3). Dependency test, on the target commit only: let d be the digest of P's `inputs` there; P satisfies a dependent when `delivered-d` exists with passed true, a listed evaluator and a milestone, and no `withdrawn-d` exists on that commit. A delivery is taken back without editing the plan by adding `withdrawn-d` with the decision reference that asked for it: P then prints `withdrawn` and its dependents are held with reason 'dependency withdrawn'. The record takes back the claim, not the code; whether the landed change is also reverted is the boss's decision and is a separate landing (RT-4.1). If P was edited after delivery, d has no delivered record and dependents are held with reason 'dependency revised after delivery' unless they pin the delivered digest. This fails closed in three cases: deliver A then publish B and withdraw B, deliver A then publish B and never deliver it (RT-3.1), and deliver A then withdraw A at the same digest (RT-4.1). Named consequence: a delivered plan is frozen; follow-up work is a new plan. What the test still does not prove is in K3 and K11.
design.changed: the dependency test now requires that no withdrawn record exists at the delivered digest (RT-4.1)

design.rule: The board is a generated file committed in the repository; a command adds the live overlay.
design.detail: D-ADR0079 point 1 puts the board in the repository and says it is generated, never hand-edited. The committed board (path from the fgos convention door) holds durable facts only: per backlog outcome its covering plans, per plan one label and its dependency ids and digest. Never a holder, machine, case liveness or failure text. Merge rule: a work branch never commits the board file. The landing step regenerates it from the merged tree inside the landing commit, so two branches cannot conflict on it; a change made straight on the target regenerates it in that same commit. On a branch, CI runs the generator in check mode only (it must produce a board from the merged sources and writes nothing); on the target, CI checks drift. Where a landing is made by a host merge button that cannot run the generator, the same check adds a regeneration commit right after; that is safe for the board because it holds only derived facts, and it is not allowed for a `delivered` record (D5). A git merge driver was considered and not chosen: a driver is defined in each clone's git configuration, not in the repository, so it does not travel with the project (reviewer/1 finding 2). The same tool run as a command adds running, engine-unknown and open exceptions from D11. One vocabulary, printed in this precedence: invalid, withdrawn (a withdrawn record exists for the current digest; shown as 'withdrawn after delivery' when a delivered record exists at that digest too), draft, stale (a published record exists but not for the current digest), published (not yet validated), held (with reason: returned, dependency, dependency withdrawn, validation aged, conflicting writes), eligible, running (overlay only), delivered. `ready` is the name for published plus validated and prints as held or eligible; `admitted` is the engine's word and the board never prints it (RT-3.5). The role packet is the command's per-plan JSON output plus the plan files.
design.changed: committed generated board is now the default (was command-only); vocabulary and precedence fixed; `withdrawn` is a printed label above draft (RT-4.1); branches never commit the board, the landing step regenerates it (reviewer/1 finding 2)

design.rule: Upkeep has three parts, and the third one records what it finds.
design.detail: (a) Transactional: whoever changes a source runs the check and commits source and record together; the board is regenerated in the landing commit (D6). (b) CI on changes under the plans and backlog paths: fails only the affected plan; old unrelated debt is reported, not blocking. (c) Sweep: a timer-run command, no LLM, exits each run; it reads the board and the run facts of D11 and appends one deduplicated exception event per plan, digest and kind through the Event Store door, with the role that owns the next action. Age since the run-opened fact is detectable from the first day. For a run with no settle fact the sweep also reads the engine by the recorded id and is the backstop observer of D12. Whether that read tells a healthy run from a stuck one is not shown (K2). The first packet's sweep wrote nothing and had no recorded start to measure from (RT-3.6).
design.changed: the board is regenerated at landing (reviewer/1 finding 2); the sweep is the backstop observer (RT-4.2)

design.rule: Each role is one short invocation with one obligation and a named file kind it may add.
design.detail: boss: backlog rows, priority, owner decisions. shaper: discussion to locked decisions in the plan directory. planner: plan.md and envelope, `published` and `withdrawn` records. validation unit (read-only fgos run): its report only. validation tick (non-LLM tool process that called `fgos run` and waits for it to return): adds `validated` or `returned` (D4). supervisor tick: select one eligible plan, start it, record the run-opened fact (D11), exit. leader and workers: inside the case only, through fgos run; they never touch the portfolio. landing step: a separate invocation that lands and writes `delivered` in the landing commit and regenerates the board; who sees that the case passed and starts it is D12. watcher: the sweep. The first packet gave the supervisor two obligations across time (start, then return at landing); they are now two invocations and no session has to remember to come back (RT-3.3).
design.changed: validation record writer named once; the start of the landing step refers to D12 (RT-4.2)

design.rule: Existing surfaces are left, not rewritten.
design.detail: Legacy plan frontmatter untouched. The hand-kept program board keeps its log as history; its lane table stops being the eligibility signal once the generated board covers those lanes, and the AGENTS.md instruction changes in that same change (D-ADR0079 says the board is never hand-edited, so this is now a direction, not an option). scripts/check-backlog-reconciliation.mjs is a separate audit of backlog rows against RECONCILIATION.md, neither used nor silenced by the portfolio.
design.changed: program-board replacement is now a direction

design.rule: Placement: this repository's tool first, then fgOS.
design.detail: P1: portfolio data (D1 to D5), generated board and check. P2: manual supervisor tick. P3: leader plus solo workers with the pilot's measures. All three as tools/plan-supervisor promoted from origin/plan-supervisor-prototype. From the prototype keep the generated-board idea, dependency checks, test cases and friction measures; replace its line parser (drops block-style lists) with readFrontmatter, its 30-minute TTL lock with holder-lock, its home-directory state and claim queue with D11, and do not carry its status words (`todo`, alias `done`). Tool thresholds stay tool options while it is a repository tool; on the move into fgOS they become config-standard keys with doctor rows (install gate in AGENTS.md). Move when the measures in named default N9 are in and one project other than fgOS has used it (mission 1).
design.changed: new; the first packet rejected the prototype outright

design.rule: Run state goes through fgOS doors: facts in the Event Store, exclusion in holder-lock.
design.detail: The supervisor tick takes a holder-lock for portfolio selection, re-reads the board on the target, starts the case or unit, appends a run-opened fact {plan, digest, case or unit run id, base} to the Event Store in the `project` scope, releases and exits. The landing step and the validation tick append the matching settle facts. The board overlay and the sweep read these facts and query the engine by the recorded id, never by planCaseSlug. This gives the board the engine key before delivery, which the first packet lacked (RT-3.2). Limits read from source: holder-lock is kernel locks on one machine (component-boundary.md:86), so it stops two ticks on one machine, not on two; Event Store facts reach another machine only after seal, push and fetch (event-store/spec.md:49, 63, 202); and that spec records the owner's 2026-10-17 decision that claims and leases are runtime state outside the event store, so the fact is history, not the claim. Named default N10 covers the gap; question Q4 asks the owner to record the placement D-ADR0079 left open. How the tool reaches the two doors, read now: `fgos events` offers sync, status, seal and export and no append; `fgos lock` offers fence, and `fgos lock-status` reports; neither CLI lets a caller append an event or take a lock. The Event Store consumer manifest (packages/event-store/contracts/consumers.v1.json) registers work, porting and identity among its consumers and no portfolio consumer, and the tester of the previous revision reports that the spec refuses unregistered event types. So P2 has a named gate: a registered event contract for the run facts, a registered lock name for portfolio selection, and a way to reach both. While it is a repository tool it imports the two facades from inside this repository, subject to the import guard of docs/architecture-manifest.json; on the move into fgOS it uses a CLI verb, which a consuming project needs anyway. P1 uses neither door: it reads files, Git and the YAML reader and writes record files and the board, so P1 is not blocked by this gate (reviewer/1 finding 3, R8).
design.changed: how the tool reaches the Event Store and holder-lock, and that P1 needs neither (reviewer/1 finding 3)

design.rule: Continuation: the process that started a run is the one that sees it finish, and the sweep is the backstop.
design.detail: The previous revision said the landing step is 'started when the case reports passed' and that 'the tick adds the record', and named nobody who is still running when that happens (RT-4.2). Rule: the observer is a non-LLM tool process, never an agent session. (1) Validation: `fgos run` is the door that binds, runs and settles one unit and returns its result (AGENTS.md dispatch section; with --json the result is under data.results). The validation tick calls it, waits, and adds the record. It lives as long as the unit, which costs a process and no model tokens. (2) Implementation: the tool's driver process, started by the supervisor's selection, opens the run, appends the run-opened fact, and waits on the engine call. `startWorkflow` advances in the calling process until the run completes, fails or parks, or with `detached` hands advancing to `fgos workflow resume <id> --foreground` and points the caller at `fgos workflow status <id>`; a conductor case is opened with no process, so there the driver is whoever runs the proposed command list, which under the owner's roles is the leader started through `fgos run`, and the tool process waiting on that `fgos run` is the observer (src/workflow/case-verbs.mjs:100-112). When the call returns, the driver appends the settle fact and, on passed, starts the landing step; on anything else it appends an exception. (3) Backstop: when that process died, the sweep finds a run-opened fact with no settle fact, reads `fgos workflow status <recorded id>` (registry text: run state plus advance {running, pid}, case milestones, closable; 'a conductor case [is running] while an attempt of its is alive') and either starts the next step or appends an exception. So the worst delay from a finished run to its next step is one sweep interval. Not proven: the status read was taken from the command registry text and was not exercised; that its output tells passed from failed and parked precisely enough to start a landing is unverified; the sweep's own write path is the Event Store append gated in D11; and a tick that dies after the engine start and before the run-opened append leaves a run no fact names (tester of the previous revision, REV-2; recorded as F27, open). The supervisor role stays short: it selects and exits; the waiting is done by the tool process.

not_included: claims, slots, leases or settlement inside portfolio files (engine side, D-ADR0076)
anything that must travel with the project stored only in Work (D-ADR0079)
a standing LLM session for any role
a new engine verb for validation (D4 uses the existing fgos run door)

red_team_answers.finding: RT-3.1 delivery predicate stays true after withdraw and after a newer unpublished revision
red_team_answers.disposition: accepted; the correction of the withdraw half is new in this revision and unreviewed
red_team_answers.answer: The predicate now tests the plan's current digest on the target commit, requires passed true, and requires that no withdrawn record exists at that digest (D5). The two newer-revision cases held the dependents in the previous revision already; the withdraw half did not, as RT-4.1 showed, and is corrected here. The first packet's F4 'resolved' was wrong, and so was the previous revision's plain 'accepted' for this finding.
red_team_answers.still_open: The test re-hashes the plan's files, not the delivered code. A later change to the delivered code that is not a revert of the landing commit is not seen (K11).

red_team_answers.finding: RT-3.2 no case id before delivery; two supervisors can both start; `held` after failed validation is not durable
red_team_answers.disposition: accepted in part (was 'accepted'; narrowed after RT-4.2)
red_team_answers.answer: Run-opened facts through the Event Store give the board the engine key from the start; a holder-lock serializes selection on one machine (D11). A failed validation is a committed `returned-<digest>` record, so it survives the 14-day case prune and clears only when the plan is revised (D3, D4).
red_team_answers.still_open: Two machines can still both start the same plan between sync points (K9, N10, Q4). A repository tool cannot append to the Event Store through the CLI today and no portfolio consumer is registered (D11), so the run-opened fact is a P2 gate, not a working mechanism. Who adds the `validated` or `returned` record is now one process (D4, D12), but the backstop for a tick that died rests on a status read that was not exercised. A tick that dies between the engine start and the run-opened append leaves a run that no fact names, on one machine too (tester REV-2, F27).

red_team_answers.finding: RT-3.3 'travels with the landing' contradicts the commit door and Q3; supervisor has two obligations
red_team_answers.disposition: accepted in part (was 'accepted'; narrowed after RT-4.2)

'Started when the case reports passed' had no observer in the previous revision; D12 names the tool's driver process and the sweep as backstop, and that rule is unreviewed and partly unverified (K13).

red_team_answers.answer: Writers are per record kind (D8); one printed vocabulary with precedence (D6); digest over committed bytes at a named commit, so two worktrees agree (D3); draft wins on day one and required-field checks apply at publish (D2); record files replace the shared log (D3).

red_team_answers.finding: RT-3.6 the sweep does not see the stall it was added for and leaves no durable report
red_team_answers.answer: The sweep now has a recorded start (run-opened fact) and records exceptions (D7c), so 'opened longer than the threshold with no settle fact' is detectable.

That was too strong: `fgos workflow status <id>` is described in the command registry as returning run state and advance {running, pid}, and the tester of the previous revision points at it and at Run Supervisor probes. What is missing is the link from a plan to the case or unit id (D11 supplies it once its gate is met) and proof that 'running' means healthy progress; until then age stays the proxy and will give false alarms on long runs. How the exception reaches a person is Work's job under D-ADR0079 and no channel was verified. The previous revision's 'thirteen execution-read-door branches' was wrong (RT-4.3): this checkout's remote-tracking refs show six heads under origin (execution-read-door/integration, /p01, /p13, /p15, plan/execution-read-door, plan/execution-read-door-decisions), three of them also as local branches. None was inspected, so whether they supply a further read is unknown (K2).

named_defaults.default: The board is a generated committed file of durable facts; the same tool as a command adds the live overlay. Branches do not commit it; see N14. (changed)
No `published` record means draft; old plans are not edited.

Subject is an explicit non-empty list of repo-relative files declared in plan.md, with no patterns, digested over committed bytes; publishing refuses a dirty or symlinked subject and any entry under the plan's records folder or naming the board file. (changed)
Backlog findings are advisory; only a plan's own contradiction or an undelivered dependency holds that plan.
Unknown engine state prints engine-unknown and never frees a plan.
Plan-first applies to all work with no size exemption, as the owner stated; shown as not enforced until the engine doors change.
The sweep is a timer-run command, no LLM; it writes nothing to portfolio files and appends exception events through the Event Store door. (changed)
Plans and backlog paths come from config and the fgos convention door, so a consuming project is not tied to this repository's layout.

Order and measures: P1 data, generated board and check on two or three real active plans; P2 manual supervisor tick with run facts; P3 leader and solo workers; then CI and the sweep; admission enforcement last, as an engine change. Measure plan defects caught before pickup, share of validated plans returned in the case, time from failure to first report, cold-resume success from the packet alone, upkeep effort per change, and session length per role. (changed)
One supervising machine per project during P1 to P3; another machine syncs event refs before it selects and treats a run-opened fact for the same digest as held. (new)

A delivered plan is frozen; follow-up work is a new plan, and a dependent may pin a delivered digest. A delivery is taken back by a withdrawn record at the same digest, which holds dependents; it is final for that digest. (changed)
Validation ages: a plan whose `inputs` or `writes` paths changed on the target since the validation base is held as 'validation aged' until revalidated. (new)
The `records/` folder of a plan and the board file are reserved paths: never in `inputs`, never in a unit's `writes`. (new)
A work branch never commits the board. The landing step regenerates it in the landing commit; after a host-button merge the check adds a regeneration commit. No merge driver. (new)

The process that made the engine call waits for it and starts the next step (record, settle fact, landing step); it is a tool process, not an agent. The sweep is the backstop and reads the engine status by the recorded id. (new)
The tool reaches the Event Store and holder-lock by importing their facades while it is a repository tool, and by CLI verbs after the move into fgOS; P1 uses neither. (new)

reviewer_answers.finding: reviewer/1 finding 1: an `inputs` entry that matches `records/` would make writing a record change the digest
reviewer_answers.answer: `inputs` is an explicit file list with no patterns; `records/` and the board file are reserved; publishing refuses an entry under them and the digest step skips them (D2, D3, N3, N13).
reviewer_answers.still_open: Nothing beyond building it in P1.

reviewer_answers.finding: reviewer/1 finding 2: two branches that both touched the generated board make a non-interactive merge fail; the merge strategy is not specified
reviewer_answers.answer: Branches never commit the board; the landing step regenerates it in the landing commit; CI on a branch runs the generator in check mode only; a host merge button is followed by a regeneration commit; a merge driver is not chosen because it lives in per-clone git configuration (D6, D7a, N14).
reviewer_answers.still_open: Between a host-button merge and its regeneration commit the board on the target is stale for one commit (K10). Whether this repository's landings go through a step that can run the generator was not checked with whoever performs them.

reviewer_answers.finding: reviewer/1 finding 3: whether the P2 tick shells out to CLI verbs or imports library modules, and that P1 must not be blocked
reviewer_answers.answer: Read now: no CLI verb appends an event or takes a lock, and no portfolio consumer is registered. P2 is gated on a registered event contract and lock name; the repository tool imports the facades inside this repository and moves to a CLI verb on the move into fgOS; P1 uses neither door (D11, R8).
reviewer_answers.still_open: Whether the import guard of the architecture manifest lets a tool under tools/ import those facades was not checked. Adding a consumer and a lock name is a change to fgOS itself, ahead of the tool-first order the owner set; that it is small enough to belong to P2 is this seat's judgement.
